% An article with minitoc's shortext option, which names its numbered
% files with one letter: S, H, and V for the tables of a section, and P
% for that of a part. Beside them are the files of an earlier build that
% loaded xcolor, in minitoc's own format: each entry has \textcolor, and
% xcolor is not loaded here. Under tex4ht, the first section's tables
% read the files of index 2, the second section's those of index 3, and
% \parttoc the file of index 0. \sectlot reads I files, which minitoc
% never writes, in place of the V files that it writes. The stale files
% of index 1, the V files, and the .P1 are therefore guards. The stale
% files stay as they are.
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage[shortext]{minitoc}
\begin{document}
\doparttoc
\dosecttoc
\dosectlof
\dosectlot
\tableofcontents
\listoffigures
\listoftables
\part{First part}
\parttoc
\section{First}
\secttoc
\sectlof
\sectlot
Text of the first section.
\subsection{New subsection}
Text of the subsection.
\begin{figure}[h]
\centering A figure.
\caption{New figure}
\end{figure}
\begin{table}[h]
\centering A table.
\caption{New table}
\end{table}
\section{Second}
\secttoc
\sectlof
\sectlot
Text of the second section.
\subsection{Another new subsection}
Text of the other subsection.
\begin{figure}[h]
\centering A figure.
\caption{Another new figure}
\end{figure}
\begin{table}[h]
\centering A table.
\caption{Another new table}
\end{table}
\end{document}
